Operator question 2026-10-15: if an agent has stopped or its lease was forcefully unlocked, can its work be restored automatically when the blocking part unblocks, or does it need the user? Today: the WORK survives (committed branch, worktree, gate outcomes in the log; cleanup refuses unmerged work; `ddflow recover` lists it) but RESUMING is manual: someone has to notice, recover and `claim --force`, write a new brief, and tell the right agent. On 2026-10-15 the coordinator did this by hand four times (the actors agent, the log-scale agent twice, the docs agent). Build, on the planned resume (P-resume, B-res-resume), the lane ledger (ddflow lanes), the dispatcher (DX-dispatch-plan, DX-dispatch-supervise) and the wait graph (DX-no-hold-and-wait): (1) PARK instead of drop: every way an item loses its lease with work attached (stopped agent, expired lease, yield requested by DX-conflict-autoorder, lease broken by DX-lease-progress-breakable, forced claim) writes a `lane.parked` record: item, branch, worktree, the gates already passed, the last commits, uncommitted diff stat, the REASON, and the RESTORE CONDITION (the item or glob it waits on, a time, or 'operator'); the worktree and branch are protected from cleanup while parked. (2) DERIVED RESUME BRIEF: an agent killed mid-run writes no handoff, so ddflow derives it from the log and the worktree: remaining gates in order, commits ahead of main, files touched, pin files that need re-recording, the last notes and findings, and the exact next commands; if the agent still wrote a handoff (B-am-handoff, P-session-context) it is included. (3) AUTO-WAKE: when the restore condition is met (the blocker merged, the glob is free, the quota window reset) ddflow marks the lane RESUME-READY, moves it AHEAD of fresh items in `ddflow next` (parked work first, priority boost knob), and the dispatcher plan (DX-dispatch-plan) returns a RESUME action with the derived brief: in advise mode the master session is nudged (and told which still-living subagent can simply be sent the brief), in launch mode a lane is started from the worktree. Reclaiming a parked item by its original agent identity or an authorised successor needs no --force. (4) AFTER-RESUME CHECKS: merge main, re-record pins (ddflow pins regenerate), re-run only the gates whose reviewed tree changed, then merge, so a resumed lane does not redo recorded work; a parked item older than a knob is reported to the operator instead of silently waiting. (5) Everything is logged, reversible, and optional per project (`[lane].park`, `[lane].auto_resume` = off | advise | act; default advise); a person can park, resume or discard a lane with ddflow lanes park|resume|discard. Regression tests with fake lanes: a forced unlock parks the lane and keeps its worktree; when the blocker's item completes the lane is RESUME-READY and listed first; the derived brief lists exactly the unfinished gates; discard needs an explicit command. Related: B-res-resume, P-resume, DX-dispatch-supervise, DX-conflict-autoorder, DX-lease-progress-breakable, DX-lapsed-lease-merge-deadlock.
